1. I'd skip ahead at 0:31, where the narration restates the question ("So if Nina rents and invests the difference, does she end up ahead of owning?"). The hook already covered the cash and stocks results by then, so the recap and the repeated "stocks outgrew the house almost nine times out of ten, yet buying still came out ahead in half" (0:36) feel like padding. I'd also skip the limits section at 7:48 to 8:11. The screen shows a dense block of small text while the narration lists the same caveats, so it's hard to follow both. The closing recap at 8:13 mostly repeats what I've already heard, though it's short.

2. I was most engaged at 1:30, when the first house goes from "$48,410 ahead" with cash to "$485,063 behind" with stocks. The same house, mortgage and rent flip to dark with only the renter's pile changed. The stacks of money beside the house make that easy to see. I was also hooked at 3:42 to 3:57, when the street goes dark and stays dark for the bubble-year buyers.
